newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybean futures end higher on export pace.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybean futures end higher on export pace.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed higher on Thursday, boosted by stronger-than-expected USDA weekly export sales data, traders said.

USDA on Thursday said U.S. net export sales during the week ended April 3 totaled 308,500 tonnes, above expectations for 150,000 to 250,000 tonnes. The strong tally suggested recent price gains had not rationed world demand.
"The immediate availability of beans is keeping demand strong. We're certainly seeing a decent demand, certainly more than expected at this point in the season," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
But analysts and traders said futures buying interest was limited on the day and suggested the bullish trend, tied to tight stocks and strong world demand, was waning.

"We had pretty good export sales today but it was up more on a lack of selling than anything else," said John Kleist, director of agricultural research for ING Futures and Options. "There's been a change in psychology and it happened last Friday. People want to see rallies extended so they can get out of longs."
Soybeans ended 8-1/2 to 3-1/4 cents per bushel higher with May up 7-3/4 at $8.55-1/4 a bushel.
